drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna need to say 'and not untied'?
outcomeNote: The redundancy charge of the previous unit is answered.

segments.he: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: קְשׁוּרוֹת — כְּעֵין קְשׁוּרוֹת, אֲבָל מַמָּשׁ לָא — קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן וְלֹא מוּתָּרוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: This is specified, «lest you say» that «tied» means «similar to tied,» i.e., close to each other, «but not» necessarily that they are «actually» tied. Therefore, the mishna «teaches us» that it is not enough that they be close; rather, they must be actually tied «and not untied.»

moves.summary: the clause forestalls reading 'tied' as 'as if tied'
moves.about: 'tied' alone might have meant merely close together; 'not untied' requires actually tied

edges.about: 'tied' alone might have meant merely close together; 'not untied' requires actually tied
edges.proposedPredicate: respond.justifies_necessity_of — «מהו דתימא ... קא משמע לן» — answers a redundancy charge by naming the mistaken inference the seemingly superfluous clause forestalls; answers does not record that the defence is of necessity

positions.claim: the clause requires the cattle to be actually tied, not just adjacent
